title: Group Anagrams
keyIdea: Anagrams share the same letter counts. Turn each word into a key of its 26 counts ("1#0#…#") and group words by key in a hash map: one pass over the words.

approaches.name: Brute force: compare pairs
approaches.idea: For each unvisited word, scan the rest and pull in every anagram (checked with a 26-count array).
approaches.why: Every pair of words may be compared, each comparison O(m) for word length m.

approaches.name: Count signature as hash key
approaches.idea: signature(word) = the 26 counts joined with #. groups[signature].push_back(word). Return the groups.
approaches.why: Each word: O(m) to count + O(26) to build the key, one map insert. The map stores every word once.

quiz.q: Why do anagrams get the same key?
options: They have exactly the same count of every letter
They have the same first letter
They sort the same way only sometimes
So counts like 1,11 and 11,1 don't produce the same string
The word sorted alphabetically (O(m log m) per word)
